equity.level_reason: Advice-to-quit and smoking percentages are reported by race/ethnicity, education and income, and the racial difference is interpreted with language barriers and social or cultural factors, but contrasts are only stated as 'less advice' with values side by side, so the cap at 2 applies.

level_alternative.reason: The racial/ethnic difference is explicitly discussed and attributed to specific factors (language barriers among elderly Hispanics and Asian Americans); a reader counting the tabulated percentages with CIs as quantification would reach level 3 plus named determinants.

equity.equity_measurement: White, non-Hispanic is the implicit referent; Asian/Pacific Islander, American Indian/Alaska Native and Other are not reported for most visit categories (n<100) because minorities were not oversampled; 534 smokers missing race/ethnicity and 1,295 missing income are excluded.

notes: No tests are reported; group contrasts are described verbally against 95% CIs in the tables. The Editorial Note compares overall advice (70.7%) with the early-1990s 38.8% and the NCQA HEDIS average (62.5%) as context only. Survey weighting doubles as poststratification adjustment for age, race and sex.
view_issues: Tables are GIF images; OCR row '55' in Table 1 is probably '<65', and the Table 1 sample-size footnote reads 52,259 versus 152,259 in the text. 'aged > 75' and 'aged > 85' likely render ≥ signs.
